answer: Like a vine trained on a trellis, an agent economy can make each identity grow through a stake: to join, an agent must lock a refundable deposit that only matures after a season of honest work. Creating thousands of fake agents then means locking thousands of deposits, so a sybil farmer pays real capital per identity while honest agents recover theirs. An opal-grade reputation score, earned slowly through verified contributions and slashed on fraud, makes each fake identity worthless until it has done genuine work, turning identity farming from cheap spam into an expensive, slow investment.
